items.title: Angle facts
items.content: Straight line: \(180^\circ\). Around a point: \(360^\circ\). Vertically opposite angles are equal. Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal; co-interior angles sum to \(180^\circ\).

items.title: Polygon and triangle facts
items.content: Triangle angle sum \(180^\circ\); exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Quadrilateral angle sum \(360^\circ\). Regular n-gon interior angle sum \((n-2)180^\circ\).

items.title: Circle facts
items.content: Radius is perpendicular to the tangent at contact. Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre; angle in a semicircle is \(90^\circ\).

items.title: Exam checks
items.content:
Mark equal sides, parallel lines, and right angles on the diagram before solving.
A proof should justify each step from givens or established results.

items.title: Points, lines and angle pairs
items.content: A point marks position; a line extends both ways. Adjacent angles on a straight line form a linear pair. Worked example: if one angle is 127°, its linear-pair angle is \(180-127=53^\circ\).

items.title: Parallel lines and transversal
items.content: Corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal when the lines are parallel; same-side interior angles are supplementary. Worked example: if an alternate angle is 68°, its partner is 68°.

items.title: Triangles and congruence
items.content: Triangle types include equilateral, isosceles, scalene, acute, right and obtuse. Congruence tests include SSS, SAS, ASA/AAS and RHS for right triangles. Worked example: a triangle with angles 50° and 60° has third angle 70°.

items.title: Quadrilaterals and polygons
items.content: Parallelogram: opposite sides and angles equal; diagonals bisect each other. Rectangle has four right angles; rhombus has equal sides; square has both. Worked example: a pentagon interior-angle sum is \((5-2)180=540^\circ\).

items.title: Circle angle and tangent properties
items.content: The angle in a semicircle is 90°. A radius meets a tangent at 90°. Worked example: if a radius is 5 cm and a tangent point is T, the radius-to-tangent angle at T is 90°.

items.title: Reasoned geometry proof
items.content: State the given information, identify the theorem, show each deduction, then state the result. Worked example: in an isosceles triangle, equal sides face equal base angles; if the vertex angle is 40°, each base angle is \((180-40)/2=70^\circ\).

items.title: Find a missing angle
items.content: Worked example: a triangle has angles 45° and 72°; third angle \(=180-117=63^\circ\).

items.title: Parallel-line angle chase
items.content: Name the relationship before substituting: corresponding, alternate interior, or co-interior. Worked example: a co-interior partner of 112° is 68°.

items.title: Use polygon angle sums
items.content: Worked example: a hexagon’s interior sum is \((6-2)180=720^\circ\). For a regular hexagon each interior angle is 120°.

items.title: Identify congruent triangles
items.content: Match corresponding vertices in order and cite a valid congruence test before concluding sides or angles are equal. Worked example: two right triangles with equal hypotenuse and one corresponding leg are congruent by RHS.

items.title: Construct a short proof
items.content: Worked example: if two angles of a triangle are equal, the opposite sides are equal by the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem.

items.title: Triangle angle sum
items.content: Draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. Alternate interior angles at the other vertices match the angles on the straight line, whose total is \(180^\circ\).

items.title: Quadrilateral angle sum
items.content: Draw a diagonal to split a quadrilateral into two triangles. Total is \(180^\circ+180^\circ=360^\circ\).

items.title: Exterior-angle theorem
items.content: An exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight angle. Subtract the adjacent interior angle from the triangle’s \(180^\circ\) sum to obtain the sum of the two remote interior angles.

items.title: Parallelogram opposite angles
items.content: One pair of adjacent angles are co-interior angles between parallel sides, so they sum to \(180^\circ\). Each opposite angle equals its alternate interior partner; hence opposite angles are equal.

sections.title: Common errors and how to avoid them

items.title: Assuming a diagram is to scale
items.content: Use only stated facts and proven theorems; a sketch is not a measurement.

items.title: Mixing angle relationships
items.content: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles sum to 180°.

items.title: Using an invalid congruence test
items.content: SSA alone is not generally a congruence test.

items.title: Skipping proof reasons
items.content: Write the theorem or property supporting each equality.

keyTakeaways: A straight angle is 180° and a full turn is 360°.
The interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
Parallel lines create equal corresponding/alternate angles.
A diagram suggests relationships but does not prove them.
